blockers: unresolved:verify-01:The page treats as a hypothetical something three openable sources already report. Reviews of Mike Wilson's 1997 biography, opened on 2026-11-12, say what the book documents. Kirkus: he 'seems to specialize in reinventing himself. By all accounts, he grew up on middle-class South Shore Drive, but he has told reporters that he lived in the South Side ghetto', and he would 'imply he had an advanced degree in physics'. Publishers Weekly: Wilson 'does a solid job of punching holes in the myths', including that he 'didn't grow up on the streets of Chicago, as he has led some to believe, nor does he have a college degree, let alone the graduate degrees attributed to him'. Computergram (October 20, 1997) relays a childhood friend's account that he 'made up delightful and often plausible details', stories that 'glorified Larry Ellison', and an ex-employee's 'Larry always had a problem with tenses'. By the article's own sentence this weakens an argument built on self-report and helps Type 3, and invented self-flattering stories are image evidence in their own right. The Type 8 lead currently rests on four self-reports. The record (type_hypothesis.against, C47, C58) does not weigh any of this, and research task 1 calls it 'expected by a reviewer from memory, not verified'.
